protocol: Histo10b Mean-Intensity Segmentation-to-Measurement Stability external test v1.0
question: Can a training-free boundary-sensitivity score identify cells whose mean marker intensity is robust to segmentation uncertainty?
development: TissueNet TRAIN only; Histo10 original integrated-signal primary failed. Mean-intensity SMS was a predeclared secondary endpoint and is promoted here as a new frozen Histo10b endpoint.
external_dataset: UNSEG GIT, 75 images, expert manual cell masks, 0.16 um/pixel

method.score: symmetric normalized span of per-cell mean membrane intensity under one 1-um erosion and one 1-um dilation of the raw Mesmer cell mask
method.true_external_error: symmetric absolute percentage error of raw Mesmer mean membrane intensity versus matched expert-manual cell
method.matched_identity_requirement: raw Mesmer cell must match a manual cell at IoU >= 0.5

comparators: geometry-only area-span under identical +/-1 um perturbation
stop_condition: If UNSEG fails, STOP this measurement-stability topic. Do not tune radius, score, or coverage on UNSEG.
guardrails: UNSEG manual labels are evaluation-only; they do not enter the SMS score.
This pilot addresses reliability of matched cell measurements, not missing cells, split/merge failures, or de novo segmentation.
All coverages 50-90% are reported, but 70% is the frozen primary operating point.
